name: Vermont
summary: Vermont allows plug-in devices with up to 1,200 watts of combined inverter capacity per meter. The device must be certified to UL 3700 (or an equivalent) and your home needs a smart meter.

bill.name: An act relating to plug-in photovoltaic devices

watt_cap_note: Combined inverter capacity of all plug-in devices on one electric meter.
certification: UL 3700 or an equivalent from another recognized testing laboratory, with anti-islanding. Named in the statute.

utility.fees: Reported as no approval or fees; not confirmed against the full act.
utility.net_metering: Not eligible, and you cannot have both a net-metered system and a plug-in device.

renters: A House draft required tenants to notify the landlord, who then has 10 days to respond with reasonable restrictions. The Senate concurred with a tenant-notice amendment; final wording unconfirmed.
hoa: The act amends the statute on renewable energy devices (27 V.S.A. § 544); details unconfirmed.
notes: Only for homes with a smart meter.
open_questions: Whether a building or electrical permit is ever required.

sources.title: S.202 bill status, Vermont General Assembly
